newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to off, pork bellies higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to off, pork bellies higher.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb lower while pork belly futures were called 0.500 to 1.000 cent per lb higher, livestock analysts said.

Hog futures were expected to be weighed down by steady to weaker cash hog indications. Light hog runs were partly offsetting reduced packer buying early Wednesday, but concern was growing that wholesale pork prices would remain weak despite the decline in kill rates which is limiting pork output, analysts said.
Packers' margins remain deep in the red and they will continue to reduce kills until product prices firm, they said.
Although futures look overbought, underlying support in summer months may continue from expected increased pork exports, the windfall from the Taiwan pork ban, they said.
The latest CME lean hog index jumped $1.49 to $77.74 per cwt.
Pork belly futures were seen posting early gains after Tuesday's bullishly-construed weekly CME out-of-town storage report, analysts said.

The report showed an out-movement of 409,000 lbs from warehouses outside Chicago, a far cry from analysts' estimates of net in-movement of 250,000 to 500,000 lbs and later pit talk of 200,000 lbs in or less.

The light pace of hog slaughter, strong cash market and reports of exports to Japan were also cited as supporting factors. However, the market turned technically weak late Tuesday when futures fell to a lower close after setting new contract highs earlier in the session, they said.
Cash bellies traded at $85 per cwt for 14-16 lb product Tuesday, the highest level since August 27.
Japan announced last week that it was already buying U.S. pork bellies to meet needs into the end of the year following the Taiwan pork ban.
